record.paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A topological space is Baire when every countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense; it is hereditarily Baire when every non-empty closed subspace is Baire. If (X, d) is a hereditarily Baire metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace be a Baire space? The source explicitly reports that this question has an affirmative solution.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be \emph{Baire} if the intersection of every sequence of dense open subsets of $X$ is still dense. Note that a closed subspace of a Baire space may not be Baire. A space is called \emph{hereditarily Baire} if every non-empty closed subspace is Baire.
Question 4.6. If (X, d) is a hereditarily Baire metric space, must (2^X, T_W(d)) be Baire?
Question 4.6 was completely solved by Cao and Tomita in [12], and its answer is affirmative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. For each $A\in 2^X$, define $d(\cdot,A):X\to\mathbb{R}$ by $d(x,A)=\inf\{d(x,a):a\in A\}$. The Wijsman topology $\mathscr{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology for which all distance functionals $A\mapsto d(x,A)$ ($x\in X$) are continuous; the pair $(2^X,\mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ is called the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

A topological space is called Baire if every countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense. It is called hereditarily Baire if every non-empty closed subspace is Baire.

Question: If $(X,d)$ is a hereditarily Baire metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X,\mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ be a Baire space?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has an affirmative answer: Cao and Tomita proved that the Wijsman hyperspace of a metric hereditarily Baire space is Baire. (The related question of whether the Wijsman hyperspace of an arbitrary metric Baire space is Baire remains open.)

status_evidence.title: Note on the Wijsman Hyperspaces of Completely Metrizable Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Cao and Tomita showed that the Wijsman hyperspace of a metric hereditarily Baire space is Baire.
status_evidence.claim: The hereditarily Baire case has been solved affirmatively by Cao and Tomita.

status_evidence.title: Amsterdam properties of Wijsman hyperspaces
status_evidence.snippet: Wijsman hyperspace of a metric hereditarily Baire space is Baire; this solves a question posed by Zsilinszky.
status_evidence.claim: Confirmed solution in the hereditarily Baire setting.
